 Netflix Taps Roberto Stanichi to Take the Lead on Licensing, Experiences
 The longtime Mattel executive will oversee Netflix’s global consumer products and experiences business, including Netflix House, as the streamer expands its retail and licensing programs.
 November 5, 2026 
 by 
 James Zahn

 2 m

 Roberto Stanichi’s next stop is Netflix .
 Following news of his departure from Mattel , where he spent nearly 20 years, Stanichi is joining Netflix as Vice President of Global Consumer Products and Experiences. He will report to Marian Lee, Chief Marketing Officer, and oversee the company’s global licensing and retail operations alongside its growing experiences business.
 Stanichi brings plenty of toy industry experience to Netflix. At Mattel, he worked across Barbie , Hot Wheels, Fisher-Price, and American Girl, helping expand the company’s approach to franchise development and consumer products. His work included driving Hot Wheels to record global sales and establishing its Building Sets business.
 There’s already a Netflix connection, too.
 Stanichi played a role in the co-master toy licensing agreement that brought Mattel and Hasbro together on KPop Demon Hunters . The partnership produced toy lines that launched earlier this year, with products appearing on holiday hot toy lists.
 RELATED
 Netflix House Reveals ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Experience 
 “Roberto has spent his career turning iconic characters and stories into global brands that resonate across generations,” Lee said. “As we continue to build on the incredible fandom around Netflix’s stories and characters, his experience will be invaluable in shaping how those connections extend beyond the screen and into fans’ everyday lives.”
 Netflix’s consumer products business has grown considerably since its early Stranger Things Funko Pop! releases. Licensing programs for Bridgerton , KPop Demon Hunters , and other properties now sit alongside a global experiences operation that has reached 15 million fans through more than 50 formats.
 Stanichi will also oversee Netflix House, the permanent retail and entertainment concept that opened in the Philadelphia area and Dallas last year. A third location is planned for the Las Vegas Strip in 2027.
 “Few companies in the world understand the emotional power of storytelling and fandom like Netflix,” Stanichi said. “It is an incredible privilege to join Marian and this extraordinary team to help expand that fandom into physical worlds, products, and experiences.”

 About the author
 James Zahn
 James Zahn, AKA The Rock Father, is Editor-in-Chief of The Toy Book and Co-President of The International Toy Magazines Association (ITMA). He is also a Senior Editor at The Toy Insider and The Pop Insider, and Editor of The Toy Report, The Toy Book‘s weekly industry newsletter. As a pop culture and toy industry expert, Zahn has appeared as a panelist and guest at events including Comic-Con International: San Diego (SDCC), New York Comic Con, Wizard World Chicago, and the ASTRA Marketplace & Academy.
Zahn has more than 30 years of experience in the entertainment, retail, and publishing industries, and is frequently called upon to offer expert commentary for publications such as Forbes, Marketwatch, the Wall Street Journal, the New York Times, USA Today, Reuters, the Washington Post, and more. 
James has appeared on History Channel’s Modern Marvels, was interviewed by Larry King and Anderson Cooper, and has been seen on Yahoo! Finance, CNN, CNBC, FOX Business, NBC, ABC, CBS, WGN, The CW, and more.
Zahn joined the Adventure Media & Events family in 2016, initially serving as a member of the Parent Advisory Board after penning articles for the Netflix Stream Team, Fandango Family, PBS KIDS, Sprout Parents (now Universal Kids), PopSugar, and Chicago Parent. He eventually joined the company full time as a Senior Editor and moved up the ranks to Deputy Editor and Editor-in-Chief.
